Query self-hosted PostgreSQL as the signed-in user

Source: R/backend__postgres.R
oauth_db_postgres.Rd

Connect to PostgreSQL's native OAuth authentication with the visitor's existing access token. The server validates the token and database role; queries use RPostgres, DBI or dbplyr.

Usage

oauth_db_postgres(
  authorization,
  host,
  dbname,
  user,
  issuer,
  scope,
  ...,
  port = 5432L,
  sslrootcert = NULL,
  connect_timeout = 5L,
  target = NULL,
  required_scopes = character(),
  min_valid_for = 60,
  session = shiny::getDefaultReactiveDomain()
)

Arguments

authorization

auth$connection from a shinyOAuth server module, without parentheses. To select a saved authorization, pass a function that calls auth$connection(id).

host

One TCP hostname or address.

dbname

Database name.

user

Requested database role, or a function deriving it from the selected sign-in's validated identity. PostgreSQL checks that the token may use that role according to the server's identity mapping.

issuer

Exact HTTPS issuer identifier configured on PostgreSQL.

scope

Space-separated scopes configured in the server's OAuth authentication rule. These scopes are also checked before connecting.

...

RPostgres result options (bigint, check_interrupts, timezone, timezone_out), application_name, or TCP keepalive options. Authentication and TLS options cannot be overridden.

port

TCP port, default 5432.

sslrootcert

CA certificate bundle path, or NULL for libpq defaults.

connect_timeout

Connection timeout in whole seconds, at least two.

target

Token target name in the shinyOAuth client. NULL uses its default token, including for clients without named targets.

required_scopes

Additional permissions to check before use. Request consent and set the client's permission requirements in shinyOAuth.

min_valid_for

Minimum remaining token lifetime, in seconds, when obtaining a token. Use 0 to accept any unexpired token.

session

Shiny session. Inferred when the helper is created in server().

Value

A reactive function returning an RPostgres DBI connection.

Details

Native OAuth currently requires Linux, PostgreSQL 18, and shinyOAuthDB and RPostgres built against the same shared libpq 18. Other platforms can run the Docker playground. Install libpq without its optional device-flow module; shinyOAuth handles browser sign-in and token renewal.

Configure a server-side OAuth validator, its trusted issuer and audience, database roles and identity mappings before connecting. A Keycloak setup is included in vignette("postgres", package = "shinyOAuthDB").

Connections use verified TLS and require OAuth. The token hook exists only during synchronous connection opening and is restored on error or interrupt. Call con() before each operation. A valid connection survives token refresh; account or role changes and sign-out close it. Discard a broken native connection and obtain a new one through con(); resetting or cloning a retained native handle is unsupported. Use separate R processes for workers.

Try the Docker demo

Run oauth_db_demo() with Docker running to start PostgreSQL 18, Keycloak and a small Shiny app. The installed package includes the configuration, demo accounts and sample data. Docker supplies R and the native libraries on Windows, macOS or Linux.

The PostgreSQL guide covers the demo and your own server setup. Use oauth_db_demo(action = "files") to copy and inspect the Docker files.

See also

oauth_db_azure_postgres() for Azure's Entra authentication.

Other database connections: oauth_db_azure_postgres(), oauth_db_azure_sql(), oauth_db_databricks(), oauth_db_duckdb(), oauth_db_fabric_sql(), oauth_db_redshift(), oauth_db_snowflake(), oauth_db_sql_server(), oauth_db_starrocks(), oauth_db_trino()

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# Inside server(), with an OIDC client requesting openid, profile and database.read:
con <- oauth_db_postgres(
  auth$connection,
  host = "postgres.example.org", dbname = "reporting",
  user = function() {
    reference <- shiny::req(auth$connection())
    identity <- reference$identity(claims = "preferred_username")
    shiny::req(identity$id_token_claims$preferred_username)
  },
  issuer = "https://login.example.org/realms/reporting",
  scope = "database.read", sslrootcert = "path/to/ca.pem"
)
output$rows <- shiny::renderTable({
  connection <- con()
  DBI::dbGetQuery(connection, "SELECT current_user")
})
} # }
